title: slot-stabilizer-reservoir-and-util-lucidity-probe
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Introduces a sustained reserve allocator to provide predictable throughput floors for Dedicated fleets; adds a linearized utilization probe to improve telemetry quality and alerting for burst events. Backwards-compatible config flags added to dedicated fleet values. No user-facing API changes.
body: Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally experience long low-utilization tails followed by sudden bursts that invalidate short-window autoscaler signals. Customers need stronger 'sustained throughput' guarantees for service classes (e.g. search-heavy tenants) while preserving overall fleet efficiency. This PR introduces two cooperating mechanisms: 1) a Slot Stabilizer Reservoir (sustained reserve allocator) that keeps transient capacity earmarked for tenants that have recent sustained demand patterns; and 2) a Utilization Lucidity Probe (linearized-util telemetry exporter) that emits smoothed, commit-keyed utilization snapshots and HDR-backed burst samples to improve autoscaler decisions and SLA reporting. Summary of changes: - New allocator implementation (pkg/autoscaler/sustained_reserve_allocator.go) implementing a reservoir that tracks sustained demand by exponential foothold windows and awards soft-slot reservations that can be reclaimed under strict overcommit. - Soft-decline controller (pkg/autoscaler/proportional_decline.go) that gently scales back reservations when global pressure rises, with hysteresis and decay-factor controls. - Telemetry probe (telemetry/linearized_util_lucidity.go) that normalizes multi-window utilization into linearized percentiles and emits HDR sketches for burst rates; integrates with metrics exporter and disk-backed transient buffer for outage resilience. - Helm values and config knobs (deploy/helm/values/dedicated.yaml) to enable/disable feature gates per pool and tune window/decay parameters. - Observability (observability/dashboards/sustained_reserve.json) with per-tenant reservation heatmap, reservation reclaim events, and burst HDR percentiles. - CLI tooling (cmd/ctl/reserve_inspect.go) to inspect current reservoir state and simulate reservation grants. - Tests: unit and integration tests covering allocator safety bounds, reclamation paths, and telemetry invariants. Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag default=false. 2) Canary in a single Dedicated pool for 72h with detailed telemetry enabled. 3) Gradual opt-in for customers requiring sustained throughput guarantees with opt-out path. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (docs/design/sustained-reserve.md) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests for reclaim behavior - [x] Telemetry integration and dashboard - [x] Helm chart values and migration notes - [x] Backwards compatibility validated - [x] Manual canary run plan documented (Linear: ENG-9244) Related: ENG-9312 (autoscaler signal fidelity work), SUP-4472 (customer support case for search tenant burst regressions). Migration notes: existing Dedicated fleets will not be affected until feature flag enabled in values.dedicated.reservoir.enabled. When enabled, there is a brief reconciliation window (up to 30s) while the allocator backfills soft reservations; this is safe but may temporarily increase observed unused slots in dashboards. Implementation details and knobs are documented in docs/design/sustained-reserve.md.
commits: a1f7b9d: introduce sustained_reserve_allocator interface and core logic
b2e3c4a: add proportional_decline safety controller and unit tests
c3d4e2f: telemetry linearized util probe and integration with metrics exporter
d4f5a6b: helm values, CLI inspect command, and dashboards
e5a6b7c: fix race in reservoir reconciliation and add flaky test guard
review_comments: Noah Chen (reviewer): The allocator looks good overall; please call out the worst-case runtime complexity for reconciliation loops and add a comment about potential O(n^2) behaviors when many tenants are in probation.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Good catch — added reconciliation bucketization and updated comments in sustained_reserve_allocator.go to document O(n) amortized behavior.
Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Can we avoid emitting HDR sketches for every small sample during high QPS? Suggest switching to adaptive sampling threshold.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Implemented adaptive_sampler with epsilon threshold; tests added to ensure sampling saturation remains <1% of emission bandwidth.
Marta Reyes (reviewer): Observability note — reservation reclaim events should include tenant tags for downstream chargeback. Please add tag enrichment.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Enriched events with tenant_id and service_class tags and updated dashboard panels accordingly.
CI (integration-tests-dedicated): Initial run failed on reservoir reconciliation flaky test, reran after adding test guard and it passed.
Noah Chen (approver): Approving pending small nit on comment wording, which is non-blocking.
notes_on_postmerge: Feature gated by default. Ops to canary in pool 'dedicated-us-west-2-3' for 72h. Monitor metrics: reserve_grants_total, reserve_reclaims_total, util_lucidity_hdr_95 and per-tenant reservation_heatmap. If reclaim rate > 1% sustained for 5m, rollback flag and investigate proportional_decline.decay_factor.
manual_steps: 1) Set deploy/helm/values/dedicated.yaml: reservoir.enabled=true and tune reservoir.window_seconds=600 for conservative canary. 2) Enable telemetry buffer on metrics-exporter: build/metrics_exporter_integration.cfg -> telemetry.buffer.enabled=true. 3) Run ./bin/ctl reserve-inspect --pool dedicated-us-west-2-3 to verify live reservoir state.
testing_summary: Unit: allocator invariants, decline controller stress tests. Integration: full dedicated pool canary with synthetic bursts; telemetry validated against HDR sketches. Load test: 100k requests/min over 15m with mixed tenancy; reclaim rate stayed under 0.4%.
